links.outcome: Change in LLM output when patient race proxy name and geography varied in vignettes
links.effect: Models were 16.8 times more likely (OR: 16.80) to introduce unprompted cost warnings for 'Lakisha' compared to 'Emily,' regardless of location; clinical guideline adherence remained high across demographics.
links.quote: Sensitivity analysis revealed that 'Financial Fixation' was driven almost exclusively by Race (p < 0.001), with models being 16.8 times more likely (OR: 16.80) to introduce unprompted cost warnings for 'Lakisha' compared to 'Emily,' regardless of location.

links.outcome: Population-specific biased or stereotyped content in LLM-generated ovarian cancer care plans
links.effect: Models hallucinated financial scarcity from onomastic signals and failed to prioritize logistical solutions for rural patients; severe structural incompetence for the Black/Rural intersectional phenotype.
links.quote: By hallucinating financial scarcity based on onomastic signals and failing to prioritize logistical solutions for rural patients, these models risk imposing a cognitive burden on physicians and inducing "algorithmic redlining."

screen.reason: The study audits implicit biases and structural disparities in LLM-generated ovarian cancer care plans using simulated clinical vignettes, but it does not evaluate an organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
